courses.title: Introduction to Language and Linguistics
courses.description: Study of language as a universal and uniquely human cognitive system: What universals do all languages share and how do languages differ? An investigation of sound systems, word-building, grammatical principles, language change, dialect variation, language acquisition, neurolinguistics. Recommended but not required for an honours, major, or minor in linguistics or speech sciences.

courses.title: Languages of the World
courses.description: A survey of the linguistic map of the world, examining how languages are genetically classified and how different languages evolve. Principles underlying different writing systems and the decipherment of historical documents. Issues of languages in contact, minority language endangerment, language death and the role of English as a world language. Recommended but not required for an honours, major, or minor in linguistics or speech sciences.

courses.title: Challenging Language Myths
courses.description: Critical consideration of a broad range of commonly held beliefs about language and its relation to the brain and cognition, learning, society, change and evolution. Note. This is an elective course that does not fulfill writing requirements in any faculty or the literature requirement in the Faculty of Arts. Credit will be granted for only one of LING 140 or ENGL 140. Equivalency: ENGL 140. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Language in the Age of AI
courses.description: Examines the impact of generative AI, large language models, and virtual assistants on human communication. Includes evolving language trends, ethics, and applications like speech recognition, text-to-speech, and machine translation. No computational or programming background required.

courses.title: Introduction to How to Learn a Language
courses.description: Skills and strategies for second language acquisition, through the foundations of pronunciation, vocabulary, grammar, and pragmatics, connected to the practical, social, and personal challenges of language learning.

courses.title: Linguistic Theory and Analysis I
courses.description: Introduction to phonetics and phonology; training in the identification and production of speech sounds; principles and methods for describing and writing the sound system of a language; phonological theory with reference to selected languages; the interface between phonology and morphology. Analytical practice and seminar discussion.

courses.title: Linguistic Theory and Analysis II
courses.description: Introduction to grammatical analysis; morphology, syntax, semantics; synchronic analysis and description with illustrations from various languages. Analytical practice and seminar discussion.

courses.title: Clinical Topics in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to speech and hearing sciences, with emphasis on the clinical perspectives of audiology and speech pathology.

courses.title: Language Acquisition
courses.description: Audition and speech perception, phonological organization, word learning, syntax, and pragmatics.

courses.title: Computational Tools for Linguistic Analysis
courses.description: Practical skills for analyzing language using the Python programming language and relevant packages. Prerequisite: One of LING 100, LING 101, LING 140, LING 170, LING 200, LING 201, ENGL 330, ENGL 331. Recommended: LING 201 and CPSC 103 or CPSC 110 (or other programming experience).

courses.title: Introduction to Studies in Second Language Acquisition
courses.description: Linguistic systems that learners of an additional language develop as they approximate towards the target language, and key questions about what this 'interlanguage' system reveals about how we learn languages. Prerequisite: One of LING 100, LING 101, LING 140, LING 170.

prereq.text: One of LING 100, LING 101, LING 140, LING 170

courses.title: Studies in Grammar
courses.description: Introduction to syntactic analysis and theory, with emphasis on description and analysis of data from a wide variety of languages. Prerequisite: LING 201.

courses.title: The Languages of Africa
courses.description: Linguistic survey of the languages of Africa, including typological and historical connections between languages, individual and comparative surveys of sound systems, word structures, sentence structures, semantics, and sociolinguistic properties of a representative selection of languages. Credit will only be granted for one of LING 308 or AFST 308. Equivalency: AFST 308.

courses.title: Studies in Phonology
courses.description: Introduction to phonological analysis and theory, with a strong emphasis on description and analysis of data from a wide variety of languages. Prerequisite: LING 200.

courses.title: Introduction to Linguistic Phonetics and Speech Science
courses.description: The articulatory and acoustic properties of speech production and perception, including practice in phonetic transcription, instrumental recording, and the analysis of normal speech. Prerequisite: LING 200

courses.title: Instrumental Phonetics
courses.description: Physiological and/or acoustic phonetics. Focus on experimental methods and analysis techniques. Topics may include: source-filter theory; spectral and temporal acoustic analysis, inter-articulator timing and motor coordination. Prerequisite: LING 200. Recommended: LING 313

courses.title: Sociolinguistics
courses.description: The systematic study of language as a social phenomenon. Credit will be granted for only one of LING 445 or 315. Prerequisite: All of LING 200, LING 201.

courses.title: Historical Linguistics
courses.description: How and why languages change over time, and how languages can be grouped into families based on historical relationships. Methods of comparative and internal reconstruction of phonological, morphological, syntactic, semantic change. Social factors in language change. Not offered every year. Prerequisite: LING 200 and LING 201.

courses.title: Introduction to Semantics
courses.description: The analysis and theory of linguistic meaning with emphasis on formal techniques for semantic analysis and their application to empirical phenomena in language, including pragmatics. Prerequisite: LING 201.

courses.title: Research Methods for Linguistics
courses.description: Research methods used in linguistics and speech science. Emphasis on scientific reasoning, critical thinking, experimental design, and the ethics and methods of linguistic data-collection. Prerequisite: All of LING 200, LING 201.

courses.title: Computational Models of Language
courses.description: A re-examination of major areas of linguistics from a computational perspective, including popular formalisms and algorithms associated with morphology, syntax, semantics, and discourse. Prerequisite: LING 242 and one of LING 201, ENGL 331 and one of STAT 200, STAT 203, STAT 251, STAT 302, MATH 302, PSYC 218.

prereq.text: LING 242 and one of LING 201, ENGL 331 and one of STAT 200, STAT 203, STAT 251, STAT 302, MATH 302, PSYC 218

courses.title: Pragmatics
courses.description: Selected topics in pragmatics and information structure, including variations in their cross-linguistic expression and the corresponding influence of sentence form on context. Prerequisite: One of LING 201, ENGL 331, PHIL 220, PHIL 222.

prereq.text: One of LING 201, ENGL 331, PHIL 220, PHIL 222

courses.title: Morphology
courses.description: Analytic and theoretical consideration of the interrelation of word formation, sound patterning, and meaningful sentence structure. Not offered every year. Prerequisite: All of LING 300, LING 311. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Advanced Phonology
courses.description: Current issues in phonological theory. Prerequisite: LING 311. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Language Across Time, Geography, and Society
courses.description: A cross-linguistic exploration of language change, discussing theories, data, and methods. Topics can include change across historical time periods, lifespan; change across regions, within areas; change due to language contact and other social and cultural factors. Prerequisite: One of LING 319, LING 315, LING 445, ENGL 318, ENGL 319, ENGL 324 and two of LING 300, LING 311, LING 313, LING 327.

courses.title: Introduction to Linguistics
courses.description: General background to linguistic studies; the different approaches to the analysis of languages; synchronic and diachronic linguistics; phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics. Not available for credit toward a Major or Honours program in Linguistics.

courses.title: Advanced Syntax
courses.description: Current issues in syntactic theory. Prerequisite: LING 300.

courses.title: Advanced Semantics
courses.description: Current issues in semantic theory. Prerequisite: One of LING 327, PHIL 220, PHIL 222. A basic introduction to syntax is recommended (e.g., LING 100, LING 201, or ENGL 331). This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
courses.recommended: A basic introduction to syntax is recommended (e.g., LING 100, LING 201, or ENGL 331)

courses.title: Honours Seminar in Linguistics
courses.description: Research papers on general linguistic topics to be read and discussed.

courses.title: Field Methods I
courses.description: Elicitation, transcription, organization, and analysis of linguistic data from a native speaker of a language not commonly studied. Practical experience in the use of fieldwork equipment. Prerequisite: All of LING 300, LING 311.

courses.title: Field Methods II
courses.description: Elicitation, transcription, organization, and analysis of linguistic data from a native speaker of a language not commonly studied. Practical experience in the use of fieldwork equipment. Prerequisite: LING 431.

courses.title: Indigenous Languages of the Americas
courses.description: Survey of the Indigenous languages of the Americas. Genetic classification and areal similarities. Structures of representative languages. The present status of Indigenous languages in the Americas, language shift, and reclamation. (Note: this course is not necessarily offered every year.)

courses.title: Community-based Language Research
courses.description: Research methods and partnerships, ethical paradigms, the social, cultural and historical context of language research, and the relation of language research to pedagogy, policy and planning.

courses.title: Language as a Social Instrument
courses.description: Language as a tool that shapes and is shaped by technology, media, politics and power relations in society. Considers multiple levels of linguistic structure from a cross-linguistic perspective. Prerequisite: All of LING 200, LING 201. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Topics in Linguistics
courses.description: A capstone course for Linguistics and Speech Sciences majors, normally taken after three years of study. Individual sections will differ substantially; see online Course List for detailed descriptions and prerequisites. May be repeated for credit when content is different.

courses.title: Directed Studies
courses.description: Supervisor and topic chosen by mutual agreement between student and Linguistics faculty member. Department Advisor approval is required.

courses.title: Acquisition of Phonology
courses.description: Development of the phonological system in typical first language acquisition from the perspective of diverse linguistic topics. Phonetic transcription of child speech. Prerequisite: All of LING 222, LING 311.

courses.title: Acquisition of Syntax
courses.description: Central issues in the first language acquisition of syntax, including early lexical and semantic development, acquisition of morphology, and syntactic development (e.g., word order, questions). Prerequisite: All of LING 222, LING 300.

courses.title: Clinical Topics in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to speech and hearing sciences with emphasis on the clinical perspectives of audiology and speech pathology.

courses.title: Formal Foundations of Syntax & Semantics
courses.description: Conceptual underpinnings of the study of sentence structure and meaning; core issues in syntax and semantics; the place of syntax and semantics in a model of grammar; interface issues. Prerequisite: LING 520 and 525 are recommended. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Formal Foundations of Phonetics & Phonology
